title: I made 600+ fantasy weapon and armor icons with Google Flow, and the hard part was keeping the whole set consistent - curious what you think
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
It's a full fantasy weapon and armor set: 38 item types across 8 factions with 2 designs each, so 608 icons total. Generated with Google Flow, then cut out and cleaned up by hand in Photoshop.  
  
The thing I cared about most was consistency - making 608 icons feel like one set instead of 608 separate generations. What helped:  
  
\- Generating 16 at a time as a single 4x4 sheet, so everything in a batch shares the same style, lighting and proportions.  
\- The exact same style description in every prompt, word for word, so the look doesn't drift between batches.  
\- A faction system: each faction keeps a fixed palette, materials and motifs across every item type, and only the shape of the object changes - so one faction's gear all matches, while the 8 factions stay clearly distinct from each other.  
  
Curious what people here think - does the consistency actually hold up when you look across the whole set, or are there obvious tells? And how would you have kept a set this size coherent?

comments.author: MiamiStarz
comments.body: the hardest part will be to get those on transparent background

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/labnfbk9x99h1.jpeg?width=1522&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=d97d590698da2dc7e685d47f38e3c394d16ef632

That doesn't work with Google's image AI anyway. I run them through Photoshop, manually remove the background, sometimes also remove 'floating' details, or redraw some lines. Then the saturation is slightly increased because they always look so washed out. Finally, I run them through my own self-built tool, which automatically splits and exports them individually. Sure, you could use AI for that, but it costs tokens and when you make that many of them, they run out quickly.

replies.author: Tough-Requirement707
replies.body: chatgpt can turn those to real transparent background png or render them on greenscreen directly when prompting, even the free version, after thats done you tell it to zip all approved images up and filename them correct. that alone takes away a huge headache part, just dont use gemini

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body: I can't confirm that, but greenscreen is the same as whitescreen - you still have to remove it yourself. With GPTImage you get a different comic style, that's the first thing. The second is, the icons do come out in a 4x4 grid, but A, they're not always centered and B, they're rotated 180° individually, not all of them. If you've ever created icons with AI, you'll know that a Codex or Cowork alone can't help you quickly, since they don't always recognize what's wrong with the image. If you build a tool like I did, you'll also be much faster.

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body: You don’t need dynamic animations, you just need a rig that tells the item where to sit, and mirroring logic(I’m assuming these will only be displayed left/right). My art isn’t AI generated, but I just use rigs in 2d for pixel art. It’s /good enough/ when customization > staying true to the pixel grid.

replies.author: Difficult_Ad_2120
replies.body: do you create rigs with ai?

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body: Yes, and then I have a tool to hand tune them. Base rig is made by Claude and then I fine tune it. Animations are also entirely done by Claude and I would consider them “passable”. Most complex rig would be a 256x256 dragon which is \~23 pieces. Took maybe 5 minutes of manual clean up to fix
